concepts.body: A reusable named definition differs from one execution of a particular version.
concepts.detail: WorkflowTemplate owns activeVersion and inputSchema; WorkflowTemplateVersion owns spec JSON; WorkflowRun stores specSnapshot, timing, status and lineage.
concepts.title: Template ≠ run

concepts.body: A node is a graph instruction; an activity is a side-effect boundary.
concepts.detail: cond/set/terminate are interpreter control flow. step dispatches a registered capability. agent/mcp/eval/shell/containerStep have dedicated executors. Human and signal nodes wait durably.
concepts.title: Node ≠ activity

concepts.body: An agent is a versioned persona/config; a skill is prompt text; a tool executes code.
concepts.detail: AgentSkillRef orders skills. toolKeys select capabilities, and mcpConnectionId links a tool source. The implementer supports local workspace tools; generic agent nodes do not.
concepts.title: Agent ≠ skill ≠ tool

concepts.body: A connection identifies a team-owned external target; a workspace materializes its execution context.
concepts.detail: Connection.type/config/token describe integration targets. Providers are git_repo, document, issue_tracker, record and api_only. Registered types have uneven handler coverage.
concepts.title: Connection ≠ workspace

concepts.body: A stored input can be reused across executions; the acting launcher can change.
concepts.detail: RunInput.requestedById is submission history. WorkflowRun.launchedById identifies this launch; temporalRunId prevents trusting a reused workflow ID across executions.
concepts.title: Request ≠ launch identity

concepts.body: Spec and run-pinned settings are captured, but not every configuration read is frozen.
concepts.detail: GLOBAL agent version maps are pinned; more-specific agent rows resolve their current active versions. Non-run-pinned settings and credentials can change. This is selective reproducibility, not a hermetically frozen run.
concepts.title: Snapshots ≠ total immutability

concepts.body: Temporal persists execution history; PostgreSQL persists application state and searchable evidence.
concepts.detail: WorkflowRun/Step/Trace are a projection used by API/dashboard; ActiveWorkflow tracks engineering status and spend. Those records are not a replacement for Temporal history.
concepts.title: Two persistence planes

concepts.body: A policy decision records permission to proceed; another activity writes the outcome.
concepts.detail: publishOutcome returns auto/require_approval and approverCount. The template must route that result, and writeOutcome checks the latest decision. A direct runTool write is a separate path.
concepts.title: Decision ≠ side effect

concepts.body: Signals measure specific axes; passing one does not guarantee the task is correct.
concepts.detail: Online EvalResult rows include gates, review, merge, judge, trajectory, policy and PII. The offline harness compares paired golden-test outcomes and treats infrastructure errors separately.
concepts.title: Score ≠ correctness proof

concepts.body: A trusted signature proves publisher/content integrity, not safe execution or correct prompts.
concepts.detail: Install validates hash/schema and trust policy; skills and agents still require local verification. References to deployment-local MCP IDs may need rewiring.
concepts.title: Trust ≠ verification of behavior

features.body: Execute versioned JSON graphs on Temporal, including bounded loops, signals, parallel branches and human pauses.
features.detail: The shared interpreter owns graph semantics; RunnableWorkflow supplies activity dispatch, signal waits, persistence and cancellation. A graph is not necessarily acyclic.
features.title: Durable workflow graphs

features.body: Create, version, activate, import, export, compare and run reusable workflow templates.
features.detail: A template declares an input contract and workspace provider. The dashboard offers an editor; the API validates node edges and references. Generated versions require review before activation.
features.title: Workflow library & visual authoring

features.body: Generate draft workflow specs from a description and explain existing specs.
features.detail: Generation is an activity, not arbitrary runtime code execution. Slack can draft and refine team-owned versions; a person activates them.
features.title: Natural-language workflow authoring

features.body: Agent identity, model, prompt, skills, tool keys and optional MCP connection are data.
features.detail: Template → channel → team → organization → global resolution selects the most-specific active version. GLOBAL lineage pins are frozen at run start; scoped overrides remain live.
features.title: Versioned agent library

features.body: Run a launchable library agent in a throwaway repository workspace, optionally publishing a branch or draft PR.
features.detail: Separate from the engineering template. Step and wall-clock caps, admission limits and per-step accounting apply. Delivery uses a fresh trusted container. No-delivery diffs are explicitly unverified.
features.title: One-off repository agent runs

features.body: Validate context, implement with test feedback, review, fix CI failures, wait for human merge and learn.
features.detail: The default spec repeats review after CI fixes. Its CI wait can use webhook signals or active polling; human merge is an external signal, not an automatic merge.
features.title: Ticket-to-PR engineering

features.body: Lint, typecheck, tests, build, vulnerability scan and performance benchmark activities.
features.detail: Gate commands resolve through step configuration and repository configuration. Graph failure modes can block, warn or retry; having a registered gate does not mean every template runs it.
features.title: Configurable quality gates

features.body: Split work, execute bounded fan-out branches, aggregate outputs, merge branches and resolve conflicts.
features.detail: Branch contexts are isolated and results are structured. Cross-repo epics are separate Temporal child workflows; failed upstream repositories block downstream work.
features.title: Decomposition & parallel implementation

features.body: Enrich agent prompts with past lessons, tracker/knowledge content, Figma summaries and repository dependency context.
features.detail: The dependency graph supports manifest detection plus inference; upstream checkout is optional. Context helpers generally degrade on enrichment failures rather than blocking core implementation.
features.title: Repository & design context

features.body: Approval, decision, input form and editable review nodes pause a run until response or timeout.
features.detail: WorkflowHumanStep stores context, deadlines and response data. HumanApproval supports distinct-approver counting. Workflow status remains RUNNING while it waits.
features.title: Four human interaction types

features.body: Classify an action by risk and choose automatic publication or human approval.
features.detail: publishOutcome records a decision; templates route it to approval. writeOutcome refuses a pending required approval. This is not a universal interceptor on every external write or MCP call.
features.title: Policy-gated outcome publication

features.body: Sensitive-file, shell-command, content, diff, skill/LLM-output and PII-related scanning paths.
features.detail: Some checks block tool calls; others only annotate findings. Administrator regexes execute in a budgeted worker thread. Scanning is defense-in-depth, not proof that generated code is safe.
features.title: Layered runtime scanning

features.body: Run allowlisted images as shell steps or structured stdout, NDJSON or HTTP-sidecar contracts.
features.detail: Ephemeral containers default to no network, read-only root, dropped capabilities and CPU/memory/PID limits. The workspace volume is writable; opt-in egress filtering is DNS-based, not an IP firewall.
features.title: Shell & container-contract extensions

features.body: Call a named remote tool from a workflow or attach an MCP server toolset to an enabled agent.
features.detail: Generic agent nodes do not acquire local workspace tools; they may receive MCP tools. Enabling a connection type in the generic registry does not imply readSource/writeOutcome implements it.
features.title: MCP as nodes and agent tools

features.body: Reply in threads, launch durable tasks, draft workflows and maintain channel memory.
features.detail: Opt-in capabilities include follow-up sessions, reactive interjections, ambient digests, passive ingestion, open-item nudges and organization signal flagging. Proactivity has cooldowns and budgets.
features.title: Channel-resident Slack assistants

features.body: Store embeddings and lessons with run/agent lineage, retrieve related items and consolidate similar memories.
features.detail: MemoryItem supports generic scopes and entities plus repo/channel/team/org links. Storage uses vector(1536); embedding model compatibility matters. Consolidation soft-deletes merged items.
features.title: Scoped semantic memory

features.body: Capture online signals, score workflow values, compare candidates to baselines and revalidate datasets.
features.detail: Hard floors are gate/assert/policy/PII. Trajectory and judge scores are soft by default. Frozen fixture SHAs, golden tests, rubric versions and quarantined cases support reproducible comparisons.
features.title: Evaluation & regression system

features.body: Route runs between template versions and track agent canary/control outcomes.
features.detail: This is evaluation/routing metadata. It differs from the canary-rollout template, which waits for external staging and monitoring signals.
features.title: Experiments and canaries

features.body: Track tokens and catalog-priced USD across runs, organizations and Slack channels.
features.detail: Limits exist at several scopes and execution boundaries. Agent Run records each completed model step; other multi-step calls commonly debit on generate completion. Unknown pricing may report zero USD while token usage is retained.
features.title: Cost, budgets & usage

features.body: Inspect node attempts, tool calls, LLM responses, artifacts, policy decisions and telemetry.
features.detail: PostgreSQL is the queryable application ledger; Temporal owns durable execution history. OpenTelemetry links traces to operational spans. Large outputs can be offloaded to PostgreSQL or S3-compatible artifacts.
features.title: Run and agent observability

features.body: Scope resources by organization/team, share repositories with teams and apply role-based permissions.
features.detail: Repository reachability combines ownership/sharing with optional host-permission checks. Per-user credentials are bound to their verified origins and the current run launcher. Query guards supplement route-specific authorization.
features.title: Organizations, teams & repository access

features.body: Launch scheduled repository work, template webhooks, GitHub event handling and maintenance sweeps.
features.detail: Temporal schedules also drive eval regression/revalidation, lesson consolidation, repository dependency scans and permission sync. Some jobs are off by default and need explicit operator configuration.
features.title: Scheduled automation & webhooks

features.body: Read and write Notion pages, Zendesk comments, tracker issues and Slack messages.
features.detail: These have concrete worker connectors. HubSpot and generic http_api branches in genericActions currently return placeholders. MCP has its own executor instead.
features.title: Non-engineering API handlers

features.body: Package agents, skills, scanner patterns and templates for export/install and SDK authoring.
features.detail: Manifest v2 hashes identity and content; detached Ed25519 signatures are checked against deployment trust keys. Unverified install is denied unless allowed. Credentials and connection instances are not portable bundle content.
features.title: Portable signed bundles

limits.body: HubSpot and generic HTTP API lack concrete genericActions handlers.
limits.detail: readSource/writeOutcome/runTool return ok:true with placeholder:true for several types. Notion, Zendesk, tracker and Slack have specific real handlers; MCP is executed separately.
limits.title: Some integration labels are placeholders

limits.body: A failed post-diff security gate can leave code on a remote branch.
limits.detail: executeImplementation commits/pushes first, then scans the diff and may throw SECURITY_GATE_FAILURE. Exhausted TDD iterations can also return failing tests. Do not interpret activity failure as “nothing was published.” Agent Run delivery uses a different trusted-container path.
limits.title: Engineering push happens before the critical diff gate

limits.body: The approval guard lives in writeOutcome, conditional on a recorded publish decision.
limits.detail: A run with no recorded decision is not gated by assertApprovalSatisfied. runTool, MCP and arbitrary shell paths are not covered by that helper. Template design and tool permissions remain important.
limits.title: Outcome policy is not a universal outbound-write guard

limits.body: The external call completes before the outcome-reference row is inserted.
limits.detail: A crash between remote success and local persistence can repeat a write. Concurrent invocations may race the read-before-write check. The ledger reduces duplicates but is not a transactional outbox with remote idempotency guarantees.
limits.title: Write retry ledger is best-effort, not exactly-once

limits.body: The run-start pin applies to GLOBAL lineage, not every scope.
limits.detail: fetchActiveAgent looks up active template/channel/team/org versions before applying the GLOBAL version clause. An explicit key@version is threaded through the same map, so it does not force a matching version at a more-specific scope.
limits.title: Scoped agent versions remain live

limits.body: Opt-in egress uses bridge networking, unreachable DNS and add-host entries.
limits.detail: Direct-IP traffic is not blocked by this allowlist; wildcard entries are skipped. Docker shares the host kernel, and the worker holds the daemon socket. Treat that host as a privileged trust boundary.
limits.title: DNS egress filtering is not a network firewall

limits.body: Soft scores do not automatically stop a run, and aggregate score is not the authoritative gate result.
limits.detail: decideGate blocks hard floors. judgeAdvisory:false can enable a judge threshold. The workflow still chooses which eval nodes to include and how to branch on their outputs.
limits.title: Judge scores are advisory by default

limits.body: A staging or monitoring signal reports work done elsewhere.
limits.detail: The graph waits and branches on flags, returning FAILED or TIMED_OUT when necessary. A rollback-required termination is not an actual rollback command.
limits.title: Release-gate templates do not perform deployments

limits.body: Agent Run has per-step debits; ordinary multi-step generate loops often debit at completion.
limits.detail: A model call can overshoot a checked budget before returning. The offline harness has no ActiveWorkflow ledger, and the fixture count/iteration bounds—not a normal run tier—bound spend there.
limits.title: Budget precision differs by execution path

limits.body: This explorer is a source snapshot, not an operational test or security audit.
limits.detail: Routes, schemas, seed specs and tests establish implemented surfaces. No infrastructure, external credentials, LLM calls or full platform test suite were exercised for this analysis. Test presence is not a passing test result.
limits.title: Implementation is not live deployment proof

usecases.body: A developer submits a repository, ticket and description, then receives reviewed code and a PR.
usecases.detail: Default path: context → TDD implementation → three-persona review → PR → CI fixes → human merge signal → memory. Other engineering templates shorten or add approval steps.
usecases.title: Implement a ticket

usecases.body: Run a library agent for an ad-hoc analysis or bounded change without designing a workflow.
usecases.detail: Delivery can be none, branch or draft_pr. No-delivery results are unverified sandbox views. Publishing validates the exported tree in a separate trusted workspace.
usecases.title: Explore or change a repository with one agent

usecases.body: Use schedules to launch repeatable repository tasks such as dependency updates or security triage.
usecases.detail: The dependency-update and security-triage templates are library content; schedule rows point at a saved template/version and target repository.
usecases.title: Recurring dependency and maintenance work

usecases.body: Plan work per repository, run independent work concurrently and respect dependency order.
usecases.detail: Epic children resolve each repository team’s default template. A failed/timed-out upstream skips downstream repositories; default-template success can require a human merge.
usecases.title: Coordinate a cross-repository epic

usecases.body: Analyze readiness, solicit clarification, decompose epics/stories, review a plan, create tickets and submit work requests.
usecases.detail: The PRD decomposition activity set differs from the simpler product-prd-draft Notion template. Tracker creation is best-effort. Story dependencies in the decomposition should not be assumed to be the epic orchestrator’s execution scheduler.
usecases.title: Turn a PRD into engineering work

usecases.body: Read a page, draft text, optionally run a brand reviewer and append/create content in Notion.
usecases.detail: Document templates route through policy checks and human approval as specified. Publishing appends blocks/text or creates a page; this is not a full collaborative document editor.
usecases.title: Draft and brand-review Notion content

usecases.body: Read a ticket, generate a response, request approval when required and post a public/private comment.
usecases.detail: record is a workspace provider abstraction. The concrete seeded support path is Zendesk; a HubSpot type label alone does not supply CRM automation.
usecases.title: Draft a Zendesk ticket reply

usecases.body: Directly create an issue or ask issueDrafter to structure a brief first.
usecases.detail: Connection config selects Jira or Linear, with a token and optional project default. Input contracts drive the run form and API validation.
usecases.title: Create tracker issues from structured input or a brief

usecases.body: Post a message to a channel from a reusable workflow with approval routing.
usecases.detail: Uses an api_only workspace and slack_workspace connection. Separate from the richer channel assistant subsystem.
usecases.title: Send governed Slack updates

usecases.body: Mention the assistant, continue a thread, ask for a durable task or draft a reusable workflow.
usecases.detail: General and code routes are mediated by workflow code; background children return structured outputs. Optional digests, open-item follow-ups and cross-channel signals expand proactivity.
usecases.title: Work with a Slack-resident teammate

usecases.body: Wait for deployment approval, staging status and production health before declaring a run successful.
usecases.detail: signal-gated-rollout and canary-rollout model gates, not deployment engines. No built-in deployment or automatic rollback is performed by these graphs.
usecases.title: Gate a release with external signals

usecases.body: Compose agents, MCP tools, conditions, human decisions and allowlisted container contracts.
usecases.detail: SDK bundles move reusable content between deployments. Custom domain behavior needs real connectors, an MCP server or a coded container capability; generic type registration is not implementation.
usecases.title: Build a custom governed automation
